related_questions.question: What are the four types of spinal injuries?

text_blocks.snippet: The four main types of spinal cord injury (SCI) are classified by the location of the injury along the spine: cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral. These regions correspond to different sections of the spinal column: neck (cervical), upper and mid-back (thoracic), lower back (lumbar), and pelvis/tailbone area (sacral). The severity of an SCI, including whether it's complete or incomplete, also significantly impacts the extent of neurological damage and functional loss, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: Cervical (C1-C8):
list.snippet: Injuries in the neck region can affect the arms, hands, trunk, and legs, potentially causing quadriplegia (also known as tetraplegia).

list.title: Thoracic (T1-T12):
list.snippet: Injuries in the mid-back can affect the trunk and legs, potentially causing paraplegia.

list.title: Lumbar (L1-L5):
list.snippet: Injuries in the lower back can affect the hips and legs, potentially causing paraplegia.

list.title: Sacral (S1-S5):
list.snippet: Injuries in the sacral region can affect the hips, legs, and bowel and bladder function.

text_blocks.snippet: The severity of an SCI is also classified as complete or incomplete. A complete SCI means there is no motor or sensory function below the injury level. An incomplete SCI means there is some remaining motor or sensory function below the injury level.
